outcome_detail: Narrows the gap on all three points, including the cargo test qualification the first pass skipped. (1) Currency: upstream has moved to v0.2.9 (published today), two releases ahead of the project's 0.2.7 pin -- the pin is more stale than the gap text anticipated (it named v0.2.8). Ran functionally at v0.2.9 via the official musl release binary, and separately confirmed by building from source. (2) Missing/ambiguous paper IDs: both '9999.99999' and 'not-a-real-id-format' fail cleanly (exit 1, clear stderr pointing to the alphaXiv URL); no crash, no silent wrong answer. Note that 'not-a-real-id-format' is a malformed string, not an id that is genuinely ambiguous between two real papers -- so this exercises 'garbage input' handling, not id-ambiguity resolution specifically; no true ambiguous-id case was constructed. (3) Discovery quality: `discover keyword` on a gibberish/nonsense query does NOT return empty or an error; it returns unrelated, real papers ('Generative Query Suggestion via Intent Coverage...') with no signal that the match was poor. This is a real, reproducible observation from a single probe; calling it a 'defect' is this receipt's interpretation of what a nearest-neighbour/semantic search returning its closest hits on a nonsense query means, not a documented spec violation -- softened to 'quality observation' here. (4) FIX ROUND: `cargo test` for the Rust source WAS run this round. rustup/cargo were installed into this unit's own cache prefix (RUSTUP_HOME/CARGO_HOME under ~/.cache/gap-wave2-20260923/web-research/rust/, which the isolation hard rule explicitly allows), and the OpenResearch source was cloned at tag v0.2.9 (v0.2.8 no longer exists as a distinct tag; upstream had already moved past it) into the same prefix. `cargo test` completed in 3.50s: 914 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored (raw/cargo_test_tail.log). This closes the unit-test portion of the gap for the current source tree; it does not by itself cover the discovery-quality or ambiguous-id behavior above, which are runtime/network behaviors a unit-test suite would not be expected to exercise.
limits: FIX ROUND correction: the prior receipt said cargo/rustc unavailability was 'judged to exceed this check's time-box' -- that implied an observed overrun that never happened; the accurate statement is that cargo test was simply not attempted in the original pass, because the preregistration (incorrectly) treated a cache-prefix rustup install as outside this unit's allowed install targets. It is allowed, was attempted this round, and completed in about 6 minutes end to end (rustup install + git clone + cargo test), well inside the 20-minute time-box.

The rustup/cargo toolchain and OpenResearch source clone live under ~/.cache/gap-wave2-20260923/web-research/rust/ and .../openresearch-src (host-local, not committed); only the tail of cargo_test.log and the rustup install log head are retained in raw/.

Discovery exhaustiveness/coverage benchmarking (beyond the one gibberish-query probe) was not attempted; this is a small, illustrative sample, not a benchmark. The 'gibberish query returns unrelated results' finding is a single-probe observation and this receipt's interpretation of it as undesirable, not a confirmed spec violation.

'not-a-real-id-format' tests malformed-input handling, not true id-ambiguity (no case with two real papers sharing an ambiguous identifier was constructed); the gap's 'ambiguous paper id' wording is not fully addressed.
No login/API key was used; `discover`/`paper` worked unauthenticated in this run, so authenticated-only behavior (if any) is unqualified.

cargo test exercises the CLI's own Rust unit-test suite (config, telemetry, update-checking, local job/session state, etc.); it does not exercise or validate the live discovery/paper HTTP behavior above, which remains only black-box/functionally tested via the release binary.
